links.outcome: Reading level of LLM patient explanations with generic vs explicit 8th-grade-level prompt
links.effect: Flesch-Kincaid grade 13.4 ± 4.8 to 6.3 ± 1.1; Flesch Reading Ease 23.6 to 62.4; 46% college-level in round 1, none in round 2 (paired p<0.001)
links.quote: All explanations in the second round were written at a middle (63%) or elementary (37%) school level, with no explanations requiring high school or college-level reading ability.

links.outcome: Readability and accuracy of AI patient education explanations before and after plain-language prompt revision
links.effect: Mean Flesch Reading Ease rose from 23.6 ± 23.4 to 62.4 ± 7.5; accuracy stayed high (97% vs 96% highly accurate)
links.quote: Following implementation of a revised prompt explicitly requesting explanations written at an eighth-grade reading level or lower, readability improved substantially.

unlisted_practices: Readability-focused prompt engineering (explicit reading-level instruction) for patient-facing LLM explanations

links.outcome: AI patient education readability and accuracy after readability-focused prompt revision
links.effect: Readability improved significantly (Flesch Reading Ease 23.6±23.4 to 62.4±7.5, grade level 13.4±4.8 to 6.3±1.1, both p<0.001) while maintaining high accuracy (96% vs 97% highly accurate).
links.quote: Explicit readability-focused prompting substantially improved readability without compromising accuracy, underscoring the importance of prompt design when deploying LLMs for patient-centered education in transplantation.
